  A.  YWCA Lunch Program

  Mr. Soto reported that in January, the YWCA Lunch Program provided 2, 806 to 162
  participants and in February they provided 3, 116 meals to 150 participants.

  B.  Senior Events and Programs

  Mr. Soto reported on recent and upcoming Senior Events and Programs. He reported
  that the two Social Security and Tax Strategies seminars offered in February were very
  well attended with over 60 participants each. He stated that a two-part Advanced Tax
  Planning seminar will also be offered in March,

  C.  Recreation Division Report
  Mr. Soto shared the Recreation Division Report with the Commission.

3.  New Business

  Chairperson Nikowitz stated that bestselling author, Brian Vosberg presented two Social
  Security and Tax Strategies seminars in February. He provided important information and
  the seminars were well attended.

  Mr. Soto added that additional upcoming seminars are: Home Buying and Selling, Right -
  Sizing, Sensational Organizing and Gaudy Law.
  Conunissioner Brewster suggested that Chair Nikowitz conduct a seminar outliming ways
  seniors can save money.

  B.  Future Capital Improvement  Projects
  Mr. Jones reported that the Art Room renovation has been moved to the 23- 24 budget,

  Mr. Jones shared the Capital Improvement  Projects FY 2023- 24 information  which was

  presented previously at the Parks and Recreation Meeting on February 22, 2021

  Chair Nikowitz  stated that he would like to see the Recreation  Center replace all of the

  Weight Room equipment, He stated he would also like to see the Silver Sneakers program
  advertised  more.

  C.  Senior  Services  Strategic  Plan
  No Discussion

  D.  Travel Club
  Commissioner  Brewster stated she would be interested in a travel club,
  Ms. Borba stated that a club would start, with an interest list and then the club would need a
  committed volunteer to lead the group.

  E. Older American Nominations
  The Commission reviewed seven Older American nominations,  three of the
  nominations were for Carolyn Gonim. Commissioner  Brewster stated that she
  would like to decline her nomination.

7.  Future Agenda Items:

  Commissioner Cazares asked if the following pending Senate bills could be discussed as Future

  COMMISSIONER  CAZARES  MOTIONED  FOR DISCUSSION  OF SENATE  BILLS SB- 17

  A FUTURE AGENDA ITEM, SECONDED BY COMMISSIONER  JANSSEN .

8.  Report of Members:
  A.  Chair Report.

  Chair Nikowitz reported that City Council held a study session to discuss City
  con-rinissions  and con-unittees. Chair Nikowitz stated that Commissioner
  Cazares  attended  the session  and asked him to report.

  Commissioner Cazares stated that Council has not yet voted, but key points
  were: shorter terms for Commissioners,  all Commissions  be reduced to 5
  niembers,  and all Commissioners  be registered  voters.

  B.  Commissioner  Reports

  Vice -Chair Johnson stated that: s- he would prefer the Senior Commission to continue to have
  a City Council Liaison and thinks the Senior Connnission should not be changed to 5
  members,

  Vice -Chair Johnson reported that the Senior Club Yard Sale has been cancelled. She
  stated that the alternative location of Civic Center Park was not acceptable to the
  vendors.

  Commissioner Brewster stated that she is happy about the upcoming seminars.

  Cominissioner Janssen stated that she agrees with Vice -Chair Johnson regarding keeping
  City Council Liaisons for City Commissions.

  Commissioner Janssen stated that she will reach out to her network partners to see if they
  have any services to assist seniors.

  Commissioner Cazares stated that he is in favor of keeping the City Conunissions at 9
  members and keeping term lengths the same,
  Commissioner  Cazares reported that he attended the inauguration  of Senator Susan Rubio.

  Commissioner Cazares reported on upcoming Historical Society events, upcoming
   A,

  Chamber  of Conunerce  events and CA State Legislative  updates.

  Commissioner Beebe reported that Cienega Valley Estates Mobile Home Park is changing
  from an all senior cotrimunity to all age community,

  C.  Council Liaison Report: NONE

  Currently there is no Council, Liaison assigned to the Senior Commission.
  However, Mayor Badar and Mayor Pro Tern Ebiner were in attendance. They reported on
  the Council Study Session that was held to discuss City Cornmissions, They announced that
  there would be another Study Session on March 14"' to finalize the decisions concerning the
  Commissions,

  Mayor Pro Tem Ebiner also reported that Council authorized LACADA to provide
  additional days to assist homeless individuals, The LACADA team will be in San Dimas on
  Mondays, Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Fridays,

The ineeting was adjourned at 7: 40p. m.
